question: Which of the following is the Integrating Factor (I.F.) of the linear differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{2}{x}y = x^2$?
explanation:
The standard form is $\frac{dy}{dx} + P(x) y = Q(x)$, where $\text{I.F.} = e^{\int P(x)dx}$.

Here, $P(x) = \frac{2}{x}$.

$\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \frac{2}{x} dx}$

$= e^{2 \ln|x|}$

$= e^{\ln|x^2|}$

$= |x|^2 = x^2$ (for $x>0$)

So, answer is $x^2$.
